title: Runbook: Restoring the Student Records Server from Backup

headings.text: Runbook: Restoring the Student Records Server from Backup
4. Stop the service and mount the backup

key_sentences: This runbook describes how to restore the student records service after a disk failure or data corruption on the primary server.
Follow the steps in order and record each completed step in the change ticket.
A restore replaces every record changed since the last backup, and changes made by registry staff during the day would be lost.
Choose the most recent archive taken before the fault was noticed.
After a restore the backup schedule must still be active.
Keeping 21 days of archives needs about 40 GB on the backup storage.
If the health check fails twice, stop and escalate to the on-call infrastructure engineer.
Do not attempt a second restore without their approval.

tables.caption: Servers that take part in the backup and restore cycle

list_items.text: Announce the maintenance window to the registry office at least 24 hours in advance.
Check that the most recent backup completed without errors in the backup report.
Make sure you have console access to rec-prod-01 in case the network fails.
Ask a member of the registry office to open three recent student files and confirm that they are complete.
Unmount the backup disk with sudo umount /mnt/backup.
Close the change ticket and note the archive date that was restored.

code:
sudo systemctl stop recordsd
sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/backup
ls -lh /mnt/backup/records/

cd /var/lib/records
sudo tar -xzf /mnt/backup/records/records-2025-11-02.tar.gz --strip-components=1
sudo chown -R records:records /var/lib/records
sudo systemctl start recordsd

# /etc/recordsd/backup.yaml
schedule: "30 1 * * *"
target: /mnt/backup/records
retention_days: 21
compress: gzip
notify:
  email: it-alerts@eastfield-college.example
  on_failure_only: true
notes: The YAML listing shows line numbers 1 to 8 in a gutter; they are generated by CSS and are NOT part of the code. Indentation inside the YAML (two spaces before 'email' and 'on_failure_only') is significant. Inline code spans (rec-prod-01, records-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz, sudo umount /mnt/backup) are part of the body sentences and are not listed as code blocks. Addresses use the 192.0.2.0/24 documentation range. 'Warning:' and 'Note:' boxes are body text.
